annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete local paper for the missing-tier audit, rechecked its mixed-radix FFT model, one- and multidimensional proofs, and compared them with the full frozen Mathlib and NumStability baselines; the existing T3 was retained after that source-level audit.

rejected_candidates.reason: These define the transform and quote a standard matrix factorization from earlier FFT literature rather than establish Ramos's new error conclusions.
The addition and multiplication models are explicitly attributed to Wilkinson and serve as assumptions for the paper's analysis.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the complete first-order formula in Theorem 1(a)
rejected_candidates.reason: It is supporting analysis for the selected multidimensional theorem rather than a separate target. Its operational one-dimensional estimate must be reconstructed inside the T3 proof; it is not supplied as a shared theorem.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the direct-transformation error matrix (3.3) and bounds (3.4)-(3.5)
rejected_candidates.reason: These are long intermediate first-order expansions used to establish local FFT-factor budgets and retain O(epsilon squared) terms; they are not the paper's final finite conclusions.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the radix-2 and radix-4 special constants in Theorem 1
rejected_candidates.reason: They are algebraic substitutions into K(N,gamma) rather than independent results, and the full statement still carries the same asymptotic floating-point model.

These local block and diagonal error estimates are supporting steps in the one-dimensional analysis. They are not supplied as shared theorems, and T3 must combine their reconstruction with multidimensional error propagation.
The maximum-error conclusion follows from Theorem 2(a) by a standard max/RMS comparison, so it would duplicate the selected result while adding only an elementary step.
Measured FORTRAN results and claims about pessimism of the bounds are empirical rather than finite proof targets.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the input-rounding extension on printed page 768
rejected_candidates.reason: The extra forward-error term and fictional-input observation are short consequences and do not supply a qualifying T1 or T2 library advantage.

T1.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. The paper's FFT theorem uses a mixed-radix Wilkinson model with independent operand and trigonometric-data errors and source-specific constants. NumStability's substantial FFT theorem instead assumes a radix-2 standard relative model, so using it would change the task; the remaining norm comparison is Mathlib-easy.

T2.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. No result matches two substantial NumStability theorems under the paper's actual mixed-radix and sin/cos error model. The only reusable coordinate and norm steps are elementary, and substituting the library's radix-2 FFT analysis would change the hypotheses and constants.

T3.decision: Use Theorem 2(a)'s product-indexed complex multidimensional FFT bound with operational nested coordinate traces, exactly represented fixed input, fixed per-axis K constants, derived telescoping and intermediate estimates, and uniform right-neighborhood O(epsilon squared) semantics.

selection_policy: Use mathematically precise claims made and proved in this paper, including asymptotic claims when their uniform quantifier content can be represented.
Reject definitions, experiments, delegated background, and asymptotic claims whose quantifier content cannot be reconstructed from the source context.
Represent retained O(epsilon squared) contributions by coefficients and radii fixed before the varying positive epsilon, without inventing cross-family uniformity absent from the source.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after checking the mounted frozen object baseline, not merely the broader source tree.
